'''Emil Paleček''' (3 October 1930 – 30 October 2018) was a Czech [[biochemist]], who researched how DNA can be used to diagnose [[genetic diseases]]. Paleček discovered that [[nucleic acids]] could be analysed by [[Electrochemistry|electrochemical]] research, contradicting previous assumptions from the 1950s that DNA molecules were too large to be affected by electrochemistry.

== Personal life ==
Paleček was brought up by his mother, as his father died in a Nazi [[concentration camp]].<ref name=Blesk>{{cite news| url= https://www.blesk.cz/clanek/regiony-brno-brnane/513275/svetova-vedecka-hvezda-emil-palecek-bada-v-brne-jde-rakovine-po-krku-i-v-87-letech.html| title= Světová vědecká hvězda Emil Paleček bádá v Brně: Jde rakovině po krku! I v 87 letech...| language=cs| work=[[Blesk]]| date=26 December 2017| accessdate=4 November 2018}}</ref> Aged 13, he went to work as an apprentice at the Bank of Slavia.<ref name=Blesk />

== Career ==
Paleček had a specific interest in the fact that most proteins contain sugar, as he believed that analysis of this could lead to better diagnosis of health and illnesses.<ref name=CT24-2 /> In particular, he believed that testing [[glycoproteins]] could detect early-stage [[cancer]].<ref name=Blesk />

In 1959, Paleček received a [[PhD]] in [[biochemistry]] from [[Masaryk University]] in [[Brno]], [[Czechoslovakia]] (now in the [[Czech Republic]]).<ref name=ACS>{{Cite journal| title= Review: Electrochemistry of Nonconjugated Proteins and Glycoproteins. Toward Sensors for Biomedicine and Glycomics| journal=Chemical Reviews| volume=115| issue=5| pages=2045–2108| doi= 10.1021/cr500279h| pmid=25659975| pmc=4360380|year = 2015|last1 = Paleček|first1 = Emil| last2=Tkáč| first2=Jan| last3=Bartošík| first3=Martin| last4=Bertók| first4=Tomáš| last5=Ostatná| first5=Veronika| last6=Paleček| first6=Jan}}</ref> During the 1960s, Paleček worked at the Biophysical Institute of the Academy of Sciences in Brno.<ref name=Iro>{{cite news| url= https://www.irozhlas.cz/veda-technologie/veda/emil-palecek-biochemik-umrti-dna_1810300832_ako| title= Zemřel biochemik Emil Paleček. Objevil nový způsob jak zkoumat DNA| work=iROZHLAS|language=cs| date=30 October 2018| accessdate=4 November 2018}}</ref><ref name=Lidovsky>{{cite news| url= https://www.lidovky.cz/lide/v-88-letech-zemrel-biochemik-emil-palecek-prispel-ke-vzniku-nove-oblasti-vyzkumu-dna.A181030_075420_ln_domov_ele| title= V 88 letech zemřel biochemik Emil Paleček, přispěl ke vzniku nové oblasti výzkumu DNA|lang=cs| work=Lidovsky| date=30 October 2018| accessdate=4 November 2018}}</ref> His first work there was investigating DNA damage caused by radiation.<ref name=Iro /><ref name=Idnes>{{cite news| url= https://brno.idnes.cz/emil-palecek-pribeh-0o2-/brno-zpravy.aspx?c=A140303_2040735_brno-zpravy_daj| title= Na cenu čekal vědec do 83 let. V USA bych byl multimilionář, směje se|language=cs| work=[[Mladá fronta DNES]]| date=4 March 2014| accessdate=4 November 2018}}</ref> Paleček later worked with the Masaryk Memorial Cancer Institute, part of Masaryk University.<ref name=Iro /><ref name=Lidovsky />

In 1960, Paleček discovered that [[nucleic acids]] could be analysed through [[electrochemistry|electrochemical]] research, which allowed him to explore how DNA can be used to diagnose [[genetic diseases]].<ref name=Idnes /> His discovery contradicted previous assumptions from the 1950s that DNA molecules were too large to be analysed by electrochemical research.<ref name=CT24-2>{{cite news| url= https://ct24.ceskatelevize.cz/veda/2297182-ceny-neuron-dostanou-znamy-biochemik-palecek-a-sest-dalsich-vedcu-kteri-proslavili| title= Ceny Neuron dostanou známý biochemik Paleček a šest dalších vědců, kteří proslavili českou vědu| language=cs| work=[[ČT24]]| date=8 November 2017| accessdate=4 November 2018}}</ref> It took the scientific world 30 years to understand the importance of his findings,<ref name=Idnes /> although the method began to be commonly used in the 1990s.<ref name=CT24-2 /> In the 1960s, Paleček spent a year doing research at [[Harvard University]] in the [[United States]]. Paleček was allowed to travel to the United States as he was not a member of the [[Communist Party of Czechoslovakia]].<ref name=CT24-2 /> In his last month at Harvard University, Paleček's experiments were demonstrated. They were later cited in many [[biophysics]] and [[molecular biology]] textbooks.<ref name=CT24-2 /> During his life, Paleček authored over 300 scientific works, making him one of the most respected scientists in the Czech Republic.<ref name=Iro /><ref name=Idnes /><ref name=CT24 />

In 1989, Paleček became a member of the [[Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=ACS /> From 1993 to 1997, he was a member of the [[Czech Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=ACS /> In 1994, Paleček was one of the founding members of the [[Learned Society of the Czech Republic]].<ref name=Idnes /><ref name=CT24>{{cite news| url= https://ct24.ceskatelevize.cz/domaci/2637104-ve-veku-88-let-zemrel-biochemik-palecek-zabyval-se-vyzkumem-dna| title= Ve věku 88 let zemřel biochemik Paleček, zabýval se výzkumem DNA| language=cs| work=[[ČT24]]| date=30 October 2018| accessdate=4 November 2018}}</ref> In 2003, Paleček was the speaker for one of the [[Mendel Lectures]].<ref>{{cite web| url= http://mendellectures.muni.cz/home/lectures/20032004| title= Lectures 2003/2004| publisher=[[Mendel Lectures]]| accessdate=4 November 2018}}</ref> In 2009, the Emil Paleček award, was set up by the President of the [[Czech Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=Idnes />

Paleček was still working on the Saturday before his death.<ref name=Lidovsky />

== Awards ==
In 1961, Paleček was awarded the [[Jaroslav Heyrovský]] award for best young scientist.<ref name=Idnes /> In 2011, he received the [[Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports (Czech Republic)|Education Minister]]'s award.<ref name=Idnes /> In 2014, Paleček was awarded the {{ill|Česká hlava|cz}} (Czech Head) and the {{ill|Silver Medal of the Senate President|cz|Stříbrná medaile předsedy Senátu}} awards.<ref name=Iro /><ref name=Lidovsky /><ref name=HradeckyDenik>{{cite news| url= https://hradecky.denik.cz/z-regionu/reditel-mencl-prevzal-za-svoje-zasluhy-stribrnou-medaili-senatu-20141007.html| title= Ředitel Mencl převzal za svoje zásluhy stříbrnou medaili Senátu
| language=cs| work=[[Hradecky Denik]]| date=7 October 2014| accessdate= 31 July 2023}}</ref> In 2017, he was one of seven Czech scientists awarded the Cenu Neuron (Neuron Prize) for their contributions to science.<ref name=CT24 />

== Death ==
Paleček became ill after having a [[stroke]] whilst swimming. He died two days later on 30 October 2018. His death was announced by fellow scientist Eduard Kejnovsky, who worked as Paleček's public relations officer.<ref name=Lidovsky />
